listenStatements.text: Feels both proud and nervous before the A1.1 Final Exam.
Says he is confident about grammar but worries about the writing task.
Suggests studying together in the library the evening before the exam.
Thinks listening to podcasts has helped his English improve the most.
Mentions that she reviews her vocabulary notebook every night before bed.
Has been offered a part-time internship at a language translation firm.
Encourages a friend to take a career opportunity and not let fear stop her.
Believes strong English skills will open doors in any career field.
Explains that she has not told her parents about the internship yet.
Says that every decision you make now shapes who you become in five years.
Advises students to read at least fifteen minutes every single day.
Recommends writing new words in a notebook with an example sentence.
Tells students that making mistakes while speaking is not a problem.
Emphasises that reviewing old material regularly is the key to retention.
Says that the best language learners are curious and never stop asking why.
Found conditional sentences the most useful grammar topic in A1.1.
Says the passive voice changed how he reads academic texts in English.
Prefers relative clauses because they make her writing sound more advanced.
Points out that vocabulary collocations are more important than people think.
Summarises by saying the whole group has grown enormously as English speakers.
